newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols down slightly.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Index vols down slightly.

text.p: Volatilities in major U.S. stock index options eased only slightly as the underlying market moved higher into record territory, options traders said Monday.
"We're sitting still, so volatility's coming in," said Jack Callahan, an independent market maker in S&P 100 index options, adding that volatility did pop off the open as the market dipped briefly.
By about 1145 CDT/1645 GMT, the volatility index, calculated off certain front-month OEX options, was down 0.04 at 22.09, off its session low of 21.92.
Stocks rallied sharply in early trading and had leveled off by around midday, maintaining most gains.
The OEX was up 5.27 at 842.43, about two points off its new intraday record high. The S&P 500 .SPX gained 4.88 to 862.89 after it hit a record 864.48.

A trader in SPX options said selling of puts in out-of-the-money S&P 500 futures options at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange had filtered over to the Chicago Board Options Exchange, hitting some put premiums and volatilities.
"The rest of volatility for other months seems to be holding up," he said.
The SPX options trader said the move into record ground was helping to keep volatilities firm and that a sharp selloff would likely drive volatilities down.
Traders in both OEX and SPX options said few big trades or orders had crossed, but Callahan said call selling was fairly heavy on the market's run-up as investors moved to take some profits.
"It's kind of slow given Friday's move," the SPX trader said, referring to the sharp rally last Friday that was accompanied by hectic options activity.
Callahan said put buying and selling were steady, with most of it coming from retail investors.
"We have no (economic) numbers for a few days, so the market's on its own," he said. "The market's still bubbling along and option activity will follow."

In the OEX, turnover was led by the June 800 and 820 puts, which traded roughly 4,765 and 4,380 contracts, respectively. The most active OEX call was the June 850 with turnover of about 3,260 contracts.
The SPX June and July 850 puts and calls were the most active in that trading pit.
The SPX June 850 call traded about 5,275 contracts and the June 850 put traded 3,880. The July 850 call traded 3,060 contracts and the July 850 put traded 4,115.
